title: Agreement of clock transitions
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be an alphabet, let $e:\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding, and let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes over $\Gamma$. Let $\mathrm{stopAt}$ assign a Boolean value to each state, and choose a state $s$ with $\mathrm{stopAt}(s)=\mathrm{false}$. For any counter phase $f$ other than either completed phase, any input symbol or blank, and any tuple of $k+1$ optional work-tape symbols, the clock machine's transition from the state carrying $s$ and phase $f$ equals the transition of the embedded Boolean decrement machine, with its successor state relabeled by sending a completed true phase to the body state carrying $s$, a completed false phase to the timeout state carrying $s$, and every other phase to the state carrying $s$ and that phase.
hypotheses_covered: An embedding of Boolean symbols into an alphabet $\Gamma$
A deterministic Turing machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes over $\Gamma$
A Boolean-valued stopping condition on the states of $M$
